value: 64 - 64*sqrt(3)*i = -128*omega (modulus 128), not real and not equal to any option
note: STEM DEFECT. As printed the product runs over exponents 2^k for k=0..6, i.e. SEVEN factors, the last being (1 - w^64 + w^128). Each factor is -2w (k even) or -2w^2 (k odd), so the product is (-2)^7 * w^4 * w^6 = -128*w = 64 - 64*sqrt(3)*i. Verified with sympy using w = -1/2 + i*sqrt(3)/2. Because the number of factors is ODD the value is not even well defined for 'an imaginary cube root of unity': taking the other primitive root gives the conjugate 64 + 64*sqrt(3)*i. Only an EVEN number of factors gives a real value, 4^(n/2): 2 factors -> 4 (option A), 4 factors -> 16 (option D), 6 factors -> 64, 8 -> 256. The 4-factor truncation ending at (1 - w^8 + w^16) gives exactly 16 = option D, which is almost certainly the intended question; options 8 and 12 correspond to no truncation at all. Recommend fixing the last printed factor rather than the key.

alpha+beta = a, alpha*beta = b^2, so alpha^2+beta^2 = a^2 - 2b^2. sympy solved the quadratic and expanded the sum of squares to a**2 - 2*b**2. Discriminating numeric checks at (a,b) = (3,2), (5,7), (-4,3): the four options give distinct values at each point (e.g. at (5,7): 1, 74, -73, -24) and only option C matches the computed value every time.

Real coefficients force the conjugate 2+i to be the other root. Sum 4 = -12/a gives a = -3; product 5 = b/a gives b = -15. Solved as a real linear system by separating real and imaginary parts of a(2-i)^2 + 12(2-i) + b = 0; sympy returned the unique solution {a: -3, b: -15}. Back-check: roots of -3x^2 + 12x - 15 are exactly 2-i and 2+i. ab = 45.

Clearing denominators gives x^2 + (p+q-2r)x + (pq - r(p+q)) = 0. Roots equal in magnitude and opposite in sign means their sum is 0, so p+q-2r = 0, i.e. p+q = 2r. Verified numerically with p=1, q=5, r=3 (so p+q = 6 = 2r): the roots are +/-3.6056, they sum to 0, and both satisfy the ORIGINAL equation 1/(x+p) + 1/(x+q) = 1/3 to double precision.

'Using all the digits' means every one of 1,2,3,4,5 exactly once, so the number is a 5-digit permutation. Brute-forced all 120 permutations of '12345' and counted those below 40000: exactly 72 (leading digit 1, 2 or 3, i.e. 3 * 4! = 72). For the record, the looser reading 'any length, no repetition' would give 277, which is not an option, so the intended reading is confirmed by the option set.
Enumerated all 4! = 24 orderings of P,Q,R,S and counted those where Q's position index exceeds P's: exactly 12. By symmetry P-before-Q and Q-before-P split the 24 evenly, so 4!/2 = 12.

Exhaustive search over n < 60 and 1 <= r < n for the simultaneous conditions C(n,r-1)=36, C(n,r)=84, C(n,r+1)=126 returned the unique pair (n,r) = (9,3): 9C2=36, 9C3=84, 9C4=126. Trap worth noting: option A = 9 is the value of n, not r; the question asks for r.

T_n = C(n,3) since no three vertices of a regular polygon are collinear. C(n+1,3) - C(n,3) = C(n,2) = n(n-1)/2 = 10 gives n = 5. Searched n from 3 to 59 and n = 5 is the only solution; the distractors give 21 (n=7), 28 (n=8) and 45 (n=10).

Fully expanded (1+x^2)^5 * (1+x)^4 with sympy; the x^5 coefficient is 60. By hand: 2k + j = 5 with j <= 4 gives (k,j) = (1,3) -> 5*4 = 20 and (k,j) = (2,1) -> 10*4 = 40, total 60. The distractor 40 is the single (2,1) term and 20 (absent) would be the (1,3) term alone.

The sum of all coefficients of a polynomial is its value at x = 1: (1 + 3 - 3)^1143 = 1^1143 = 1. Cross-checked by fully expanding the cube (1+3x-3x^2)^3 and substituting x=1, which returns 1. The odd exponent 1143 is a red herring aimed at the -1 distractor; the base evaluates to +1, not -1.

Take roots alpha-d, alpha, alpha+d. Then a = -3*alpha, b = 3*alpha^2 - d^2, c = -alpha^3 + alpha*d^2. Symbolically 2a^3 - 9ab = 27*alpha*(alpha^2 - d^2), and sympy confirms 2a^3 - 9ab + 27c = 0 identically while 2a^3 - 9ab - 27c is not zero. Two discriminating concrete AP root sets: {1,2,3} gives 2a^3-9ab = 162 with 27c = -162 and -27c = 162; {2,5,8} gives 2160 with -27c = 2160. Sign matches -27c in both.

value: A is the zero matrix (A = A^T and A = -A^T force 2A = O)
note: Solved the full 3x3 entrywise system a_ij = a_ji and a_ij = -a_ji with sympy; the unique solution is every entry 0. FLAG: options A, C and D are all vacuously TRUE as well, since a zero square matrix is diagonal, is a scalar matrix with scalar 0, and is square. B is the only option that fully characterises A and is clearly the intended answer, but the stem does not say 'best' or 'most specific', so strictly more than one option is true.

(A + A^T)^T = A^T + A = A + A^T, so it is symmetric. Symbolically for a general 2x2 matrix, (A+A^T) - (A+A^T)^T is the zero matrix while (A+A^T) + (A+A^T)^T is not, so it is symmetric and not skew. Checked a random integer 3x3 A: A+A^T, A*A^T, A^T+A and A^T*A are ALL symmetric and none is skew, so options B, C and D are false and exactly one option is true. Note C is the same object as A merely rewritten, but it asserts the wrong property.

From A^2 - A + I = O we get A - A^2 = I, i.e. A(I - A) = I, so A^(-1) = I - A. Verified on two independent concrete matrices that satisfy A^2 - A + I = O: the companion matrix [[0,-1],[1,1]] (its inverse is [[1,1],[-1,0]] which equals I - A exactly, while A-I, A+I and A all differ) and the 60-degree rotation [[1/2,-sqrt(3)/2],[sqrt(3)/2,1/2]] (again inverse minus (I - A) is the zero matrix). A is invertible because det is nonzero for both.
